newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian privatisation to yield 10-12 trln rbs in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russian privatisation to yield 10-12 trln rbs in 97.

text.p: The Russian government hopes to raise at least 10 trillion roubles ($1.7 billion) from sales of state holdings this year, First Deputy Chairman of the Russian Federal Property Fund Vladimir Malin said on Tuesday.
"We plan this year to provide budget revenues of about 10 to 12 trillion roubles," Malin said.
He said most of the money would come from sales of state stakes in national utility UES, telecommunications holding company AO Svyazinvest and state oil holding company Rosneft.
"If we succeed in making all the sales we plan, I think (the amount of budget revenues from privatisation) will be even more," Malin told Reuters.
The government, currently in a battle with parliament over severe budget cuts, is working on an emergency programme to raise an extra 30 trillion roubles for the 1997 budget.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told the Duma lower house of parliament last week that about half of the additional revenue would come in the form of taxes from enterprises with the biggest tax arrears and from privatisation.
The other half would come from improved collection of excise duties and customs tariffs.
A similar programme was announced last month by Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais, who said then that a new approach to the market for precious metals and stones would also contribute funds.
The government has missed previous targets for privatisation revenues.
